# Company 053 — Software Release Autopilot

**Company ID:** `company:future:053`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:053`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-053-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no build, merge, deployment, promotion, migration or rollback execution.

## Business identity

Purpose: coordinate software releases from candidate build through tests, dependency/security checks, migration planning, staged rollout, monitoring, rollback and evidence.

Problem: release steps span source control, CI, artifacts, databases, feature flags and production telemetry; manual gaps create outages, inconsistent evidence and unsafe emergency changes.

Value: deterministic release gates, reproducible candidates, safer canaries, explicit authorization, automated verification and reliable rollback.

## Complete product tree

Release Candidate Builder; CI Gate Orchestrator; Test/Evaluation Matrix; Dependency/SBOM Gate; Security/Secret Gate; Migration Planner; Release Notes Generator; Approval/Change-Control Workflow; Environment Promotion; Canary/Blue-Green/Rolling Controller; Feature-Flag Coordinator; Health/SLO Verification; Automatic Rollback Recommendation; Artifact Provenance; Incident Correlation; Release Calendar; Multi-Service Release Train; API/SDK/CLI; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Compliance Packs; Managed Release Operations.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: immutable build identity, source SHA, dependency lock, artifact hashes/signatures, environment config, test suites, quality thresholds, migration compatibility, backward/forward compatibility, rollout percentage, cohorts, health windows, SLOs, error budgets, approval scopes, rollback point, incident linkage, evidence package and post-release review.

Customers: software teams, SaaS, platforms, enterprises, agencies, regulated engineering orgs, DevOps/SRE teams and software vendors.

Verticals: web/SaaS, mobile backends, APIs, enterprise software, fintech infrastructure, healthcare admin, ecommerce, developer tooling, data/AI services. Regulated/high-risk environments need stronger approval/evidence packs.

## Brain capability tree / architecture

Brain may summarize risk, compare changes, infer likely failure surfaces and recommend rollout strategy. Deterministic release policy owns gate pass/fail, artifact identity, migration ordering, rollout ceilings and rollback triggers. Brain cannot merge/deploy/promote by itself without protected authority.

Architecture: release state machine, source/artifact registry, CI/test adapters, dependency/security scanner adapters, migration compatibility engine, environment registry, rollout controller, health/SLO evaluator, feature-flag adapter, evidence ledger, protected deployment gate, replayable release timeline.

## Agent tree

Release Planner; Change Analyzer; Test Coordinator; Security Gate Agent; Dependency Agent; Migration Agent; Release Notes Agent; Canary Monitor; Health Verifier; Rollback Coordinator; Incident Correlator; Compliance/Evidence Agent; QA/Release Manager Agent.

## Deterministic services

Artifact hashing/signing; candidate immutability; version registry; CI orchestration; migration ordering; environment locks; deployment idempotency; rollout percentages; health thresholds; rollback points; release calendars; approval ledger; protected deploy/promote/rollback gates.

## Workflow tree

Freeze candidate → verify source/artifacts/config → run tests/security/dependencies → validate migrations/compatibility → generate risk/evidence → obtain required approval → deploy to allowed environment → canary/rolling observation → verify health/SLOs → promote or rollback → reconcile migration/artifact state → close with release evidence/postmortem links.

## Integrations / API / data

Git/source control, CI systems, artifact/container registries, cloud/hosting, databases/migration tools, feature flags, observability, incident/ticketing, change-management systems, package registries. APIs for candidates, gates, artifacts, approvals, rollout, health, rollback and evidence.

Data: releases, SHAs, artifacts, dependencies, tests, migrations, approvals, environments, rollout observations, incidents and rollback outcomes.

## Monetization / distribution

Repos/services/environments, release volume, seats, enterprise/private, compliance packs, API, managed operations. Distribution via developer/DevOps ecosystems, cloud marketplaces and engineering consultancies.

## Security/privacy/compliance

High infrastructure authority. Environment separation, least privilege, immutable candidate identity, secret-free client state, dual control for critical production changes, maintenance/change freezes, migration backups, rollout ceilings and independent verification.

## Failure / edge cases

Flaky tests, partial deploy, migration succeeds/app fails, rollback-incompatible schema, provider outage, stale artifact, poisoned dependency, feature-flag mismatch, canary cohort bias, monitoring blind spot, emergency hotfix, multiple services with order dependencies. Unknown or incompatible state blocks promotion.

## Scale / overlap

Single repo → multi-service release train → enterprise software-delivery control plane. Overlap #49 reliability, #72 API drift, #80 dependency risk, #82 backup verification, #100 modernization. #053 owns release lifecycle and promotion control.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** immutable build/release identity, environment boundaries, protected deploy/promote/rollback classes, migration compatibility, canary/health evidence.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center already has deployment/release gates; portfolio reverse-map must preserve reusable release factory seams.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** provider-neutral deployment adapters, artifact registry, migration contract, rollout/rollback control.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** customer CI/cloud connectors, UI, pricing, compliance packs.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** fleet release trains and global progressive delivery.

# Mandatory 24-part completion block

1. Product Tree: candidate/CI/tests/dependency/security/migrations/notes/approvals/promotion/canary/flags/health/rollback/provenance/incidents/API.
2. Feature Tree: SHA/artifacts/config/tests/thresholds/migrations/compatibility/rollout/SLO/approval/rollback/evidence.
3. Customer Tree: software/SaaS/platform/enterprise/agency/regulated/DevOps/vendor.
4. Vertical Tree: web/mobile/API/enterprise/finance infra/health admin/commerce/devtools/data-AI.
5. Brain Tree: risk/change reasoning; merge/deploy/promote remains protected.
6. Agent Tree: planner/change/test/security/dependency/migration/notes/canary/verifier/rollback/incident/evidence.
7. Service Tree: hash/sign/version/CI/migration locks/idempotency/rollout/health/rollback/calendar/approval.
8. Workflow Tree: freeze→gate→approve→deploy→observe→promote/rollback→reconcile→evidence.
9. Integration Tree: Git/CI/artifacts/cloud/DB/flags/observability/incidents/change management/packages.
10. Data Tree: releases/artifacts/tests/migrations/approvals/environments/observations/incidents.
11. API Tree: candidates/gates/artifacts/approvals/rollout/health/rollback/evidence.
12. Monetization Tree: repos/services/environments/releases/seats/enterprise/API/managed.
13. Distribution Tree: developer/DevOps/cloud/consultancies.
14. Automation Tree: build/gates/canary/verification automated; production authority gated.
15. Moat Tree: release outcome corpus, compatibility graph, connector breadth, policy packs.
16. Platform Tree: release tool→progressive-delivery autopilot→software change control plane.
17. Risk Tree: bad deploy/schema incompatibility/secret leak/supply-chain/canary false confidence.
18. Scale Tree: repo→service fleet→enterprise/global delivery.
19. Spinoff Tree: migration compatibility/release evidence modules; reliability/dependency products remain separate.
20. Command Center Dependencies: release identity, protected actions, artifacts, provider adapters, QA, observability, recovery.
21. Design-Now Requirements: immutable candidate/artifact/environment/authorization/evidence contracts.
22. Build-Now Requirements: preserve Command Center Deployment Factory and safe rollout/rollback interfaces.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: customer connectors/UI/compliance packs/pricing.
24. Autonomous Mature State: routine releases progress through deterministic gates/canaries automatically; humans authorize high-risk production changes and resolve ambiguous failures.

## Saturation result

Further branches converge into reliability, dependency risk, backup or migration products already represented.

# Company 054 — Localization Autopilot

**Company ID:** `company:future:054`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:054`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-054-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no external publishing or customer content changes.

## Business identity

Purpose: continuously localize software, websites, documentation, catalogs, support content, subtitles and speech while preserving terminology, product meaning, formatting and locale quality.

Problem: localization becomes fragmented across files, translators, repositories and product teams; strings drift, terminology conflicts and releases ship with missing or culturally inappropriate content.

Value: synchronized localization pipelines, translation memory, terminology governance, automated QA, source-change detection and human review only where confidence/risk requires it.

## Complete product tree

Translation Management System; Continuous Localization Pipeline; Translation Memory; Terminology/Glossary Registry; Locale Style Guides; UI/String Localization; Website/CMS Localization; Docs/Knowledge Localization; Product Catalog Localization; Support Content Localization; Subtitle/Caption Localization; Speech/Dubbing Orchestration; Image/Text-in-Image Localization; Marketing Adaptation; Locale QA; Pseudolocalization; Developer CLI/SDK/API; Git/CI Integration; Vendor/Translator Portal; White-Label/OEM; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Industry/Brand Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: source/target locale, string keys, context/screenshots, placeholders, plural/gender rules, ICU formats, HTML/markdown preservation, terminology, forbidden terms, brand voice, legal strings, translation memory, fuzzy matches, confidence, human review, locale completeness, visual overflow, RTL, date/number/currency formats, accessibility, release synchronization and rollback.

Customers: SaaS, ecommerce, marketplaces, mobile apps, game/software publishers, documentation teams, support organizations, agencies, enterprises, content/media platforms and developer-tool vendors.

Verticals: software, ecommerce/catalog, gaming, media/subtitles, education, travel/hospitality, healthcare administrative interfaces, fintech UI, legal/compliance documentation, customer support. Regulated/legal strings require specialist review.

## Brain capability tree / architecture

Brain may translate/adapt, reason about terminology/context/tone and identify ambiguity. Deterministic validators own placeholders, formats, locale completeness, prohibited mutations and source/target version alignment. Brain cannot silently reinterpret legal/regulatory text or publish without the project's release policy.

Architecture: source-content registry, locale/version graph, translation memory, terminology ontology, provider/model router, deterministic format validators, visual-layout QA, human review queue, provenance, release synchronization and rollback.

## Agent tree

Source Sync Agent; Translation Agent; Terminology Agent; Context/Brand Agent; Locale QA Agent; Visual Layout Agent; Subtitle/Timing Agent; Speech/Dubbing Coordinator; Human Review Router; Release Sync Agent; Regression Agent; Analytics Agent.

## Deterministic services

String extraction; key/version registry; placeholder/ICU validation; file format parsers; locale fallback; completeness calculation; terminology enforcement; RTL/pseudolocalization checks; source-diff detection; translation-memory retrieval; content hashing; release gates.

## Workflow tree

Source change → extract/version content → classify risk/context → retrieve memory/terminology → translate/adapt → deterministic format/placeholder/terminology QA → visual/locale QA → route low-confidence/high-risk text to review → approve → package exact locale version → release under protected publishing/deployment policy → monitor issues → correct with lineage preserved.

## Integrations / API / data

Git/CI, CMS, app stores/build systems, ecommerce catalogs, documentation platforms, support/KB, design tools, subtitle/video systems, speech providers, translation vendors. APIs for sources, strings, locales, translations, memory, terminology, QA and release packages.

Data: content units, source/target versions, locales, memory segments, terminology, approvals, QA findings, provider/model provenance and release identity. Customer content stays isolated.

## Monetization / distribution

Words/characters/strings, locales, projects/repos, seats, provider usage, enterprise/private, API/OEM, premium QA/voice/video packs, managed localization. Distribution through developer/CMS/ecommerce/support ecosystems and localization agencies.

## Security/privacy/compliance

Private source content may contain secrets or PII. Pre-translation redaction/classification, provider privacy routing, tenant isolation, restricted legal strings, retention controls and audit. Accessibility and locale-specific legal requirements must be modeled without pretending the system replaces local counsel.

## Failure / edge cases

Ambiguous source, placeholders corrupted, source key removed, string reused in different context, dialect differences, RTL layout failure, font coverage, plural edge cases, legal wording, brand names, product names, subtitles exceeding timing, speech pronunciation, offensive/culturally inappropriate adaptation, source changes during review. Version pinning prevents stale localization from overwriting newer source.

## Scale / overlap

Single app → multi-product enterprise → embedded continuous localization infrastructure. Overlap #28 knowledge-base maintainer, #45 support, #53 release autopilot, #55 catalog intelligence. #054 owns cross-locale transformation/quality.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** content/version/provenance contracts, provider privacy routing, artifact localization lineage, release identity and locale metadata.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center Brain/Artifact/Deployment abstractions should remain locale-aware and provider-neutral.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** translation memory/terminology registries, locale QA, source sync and isolation.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** customer connectors, translation providers, UI, industry packs and pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** global vendor network, large-scale speech/video localization and cross-product terminology graphs.

# Mandatory 24-part completion block

1. Product Tree: TMS/pipeline/memory/terminology/style/UI/web/docs/catalog/support/subtitle/speech/image/marketing/QA/pseudo/API/vendor/enterprise.
2. Feature Tree: locales/keys/context/placeholders/plurals/formats/terminology/voice/memory/confidence/review/RTL/accessibility/release.
3. Customer Tree: SaaS/ecommerce/marketplace/apps/games/docs/support/agencies/enterprise/media/devtools.
4. Vertical Tree: software/catalog/gaming/media/education/travel/health admin/fintech UI/legal docs/support.
5. Brain Tree: translation/adaptation/context reasoning; high-risk legal/publishing decisions gated.
6. Agent Tree: sync/translation/terminology/brand/locale QA/layout/subtitle/speech/review/release/regression.
7. Service Tree: extract/registry/validators/parsers/fallback/completeness/terminology/RTL/memory/hash/release gates.
8. Workflow Tree: change→extract→memory→translate→validate→review→package→release→monitor/correct.
9. Integration Tree: Git/CI/CMS/app/ecommerce/docs/support/design/video/speech/vendors.
10. Data Tree: content units/versions/locales/memory/terms/approvals/QA/provider provenance/releases.
11. API Tree: sources/strings/locales/translations/memory/terminology/QA/packages.
12. Monetization Tree: words/strings/locales/projects/seats/provider/API/enterprise/managed/packs.
13. Distribution Tree: developer/CMS/ecommerce/support/localization agencies/OEM.
14. Automation Tree: sync/translation/QA/package automated; ambiguous/high-risk/publish gated.
15. Moat Tree: translation memory, domain terminology, evaluated locale QA, connector breadth.
16. Platform Tree: localization tool→continuous localization OS→embedded multilingual content infrastructure.
17. Risk Tree: mistranslation/legal drift/secret exposure/layout break/stale overwrite/cultural harm.
18. Scale Tree: one app→portfolio→global enterprise platform.
19. Spinoff Tree: speech dubbing/visual localization may become modules; release/catalog/support stay adjacent companies.
20. Command Center Dependencies: artifact/version registry, provider routing, privacy, release controls, evaluations, memory.
21. Design-Now Requirements: content/locale/version/provenance and provider-routing metadata.
22. Build-Now Requirements: ensure Command Center artifacts/UI/Brain can represent locale and translation lineage without redesign.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: customer locale packs/connectors/providers/UI/pricing.
24. Autonomous Mature State: low-risk content continuously localizes and validates; humans handle ambiguity, brand/legal nuance and final protected publishing decisions.

## Saturation result

Further branches converge into catalog, support, release or media-specific localization modules rather than new top-level companies.

# Company 055 — Product Catalog Intelligence Engine

**Company ID:** `company:future:055`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:055`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-055-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no listing publication, pricing, inventory, supplier or marketplace mutation.

## Business identity

Purpose: turn fragmented product data into a normalized, enriched, channel-ready catalog with trustworthy taxonomy, attributes, variants, compatibility, media, compliance and quality evidence.

Problem: merchants and manufacturers hold inconsistent titles, attributes, SKUs, variants, images and channel-specific rules across suppliers, ERPs, PIMs and marketplaces.

Value: cleaner catalog data, fewer listing suppressions, richer discovery, better compatibility, reusable product truth and faster multi-channel operations.

## Complete product tree

Catalog Ingestion Hub; Product Entity Resolution; SKU/GTIN/MPN Normalization; Taxonomy Classifier; Attribute Extraction/Completion; Variant Family Builder; Duplicate/Merge Workbench; Compatibility/Fitment Engine; Product Relationship Graph; Title/Description Generator; Image/Media Quality Inspector; Channel Schema Mapper; Marketplace Feed Builder; SEO/Structured-Data Pack; Compliance/Restricted-Attribute Checker; Catalog Health Dashboard; Supplier Data Quality Portal; Change/Reconciliation Engine; API/SDK; Embedded/OEM PIM Intelligence; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Vertical Taxonomy Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: canonical product identity, supplier aliases, category/taxonomy, attributes/units, variants/options, parent-child families, bundles/kits, compatibility, dimensions/weights, ingredients/materials, regulatory flags, media, translations, descriptions, SEO fields, channel-specific requirements, confidence/provenance, missing/contradictory field detection, change history and approvals.

Customers: ecommerce merchants, marketplaces, manufacturers, distributors, wholesalers, retailers, agencies, PIM/ERP vendors, dropship businesses, multi-brand groups and data providers.

Verticals: apparel, beauty, home, automotive parts/fitment, electronics, industrial/MRO, food/grocery, pet, healthcare consumer goods, building materials, books/media, jewelry. Each requires specialized ontology, units, compliance and variant logic.

## Brain capability tree / architecture

Brain may classify products, infer candidate attributes, reconcile descriptions and recommend taxonomy/compatibility. Deterministic identity, unit conversion, validation, channel schema and compliance rules own canonical acceptance. Brain cannot invent safety-critical attributes, certifications, ingredients or compatibility without evidence.

Architecture: source connector layer, canonical product graph, entity-resolution service, taxonomy/ontology registry, attribute schemas, rules/constraints, media analysis, search/vector matching, provenance/confidence ledger, channel adapter registry, versioned catalog state and optional grounded multimodal models.

## Agent tree

Catalog Intake Agent; Entity Resolution Agent; Taxonomy Agent; Attribute Agent; Variant Agent; Compatibility Agent; Duplicate/Merge Agent; Copy/SEO Agent; Image QA Agent; Channel Compliance Agent; Supplier Quality Agent; Localization Agent; Change/Reconciliation Agent; Catalog QA Agent.

## Deterministic services

SKU/GTIN normalization; unit conversion; schema validation; variant constraints; dedup fingerprints; channel validators; product-family graph; restricted-field rules; feed generation; versioning; idempotent imports/exports; evidence/provenance and protected publish gates.

## Workflow tree

Source ingest → validate/quarantine → resolve product identity → normalize units/identifiers → classify taxonomy → extract/enrich attributes → build variants/relationships → detect conflicts/missing fields → human/evidence review where uncertain → generate channel mappings/copy/media requirements → validate channel/compliance → create feed package → publish only via authorized downstream action → reconcile channel results back to canonical product truth.

## Integrations / API / data

ERP/PIM, suppliers, marketplaces, ecommerce platforms, DAM/media storage, inventory/order systems, shipping, search, SEO feeds, regulatory/product-data sources where authorized. APIs for products, taxonomy, attributes, variants, compatibility, media, channel validation, feeds and catalog health.

Data: canonical products, identifiers, suppliers, taxonomies, attributes, units, variants, relationships, compatibility, media, channel mappings, validation findings, provenance and versions.

## Monetization / distribution

SKUs/products, source feeds, channels, enrichment actions, API volume, seats, enterprise/private, supplier quality modules, vertical taxonomy/fitment packs, managed catalog operations. Distribution through ecommerce/PIM/ERP/marketplace ecosystems and agencies/integrators.

## Security/privacy/compliance

Product data is less sensitive than customer data but supplier contracts, costs, unpublished launches and restricted products may be confidential. Enforce tenant separation, source licensing, provenance, intellectual-property controls, no fabricated regulated claims and protected publishing.

## Failure / edge cases

Same GTIN reused incorrectly, private-label duplicates, bundles, regional variants, size/color ambiguity, unit mismatch, image mismatch, partial supplier updates, category changes, recalled/discontinued products, conflicting ingredients/materials, auto fitment ambiguity, marketplace schema change, stale feed. Unknown fields remain unknown rather than hallucinated.

## Scale / overlap

Small merchant catalog → multi-brand enterprise PIM intelligence → product-data infrastructure/API. Overlap #7 pricing, #34 returns, #54 localization, #59 marketplace listing, Morgancommerce future operations. #055 owns canonical product-data intelligence.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** canonical entity/provenance/version pattern, extensible taxonomy/ontology, artifact/media references, channel adapters, confidence/unknown semantics.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center canonical-data/registry/foundry architecture should retain generic entity/taxonomy/provenance extensibility.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** product graph, taxonomy/attribute registry, entity resolution, import/export adapters and validation engine.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** marketplace connectors, vertical taxonomies, catalog UI, enrichment models, pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** cross-supplier product graph and massive catalog knowledge network.

1. Product Tree: ingest/entity/SKU/taxonomy/attributes/variants/dedup/fitment/graph/copy/media/channel/SEO/compliance/health/supplier/API/PIM.
2. Feature Tree: identity/aliases/category/attributes/units/variants/bundles/fitment/dimensions/materials/media/translations/channel/confidence/versioning.
3. Customer Tree: ecommerce/marketplace/manufacturer/distributor/retailer/agency/PIM/ERP/dropship/multi-brand/data provider.

# Company 056 — Synthetic Data Platform

**Company ID:** `company:future:056`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:056`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-056-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no customer data ingestion, model training, data release or external publication.

## Business identity

Purpose: generate statistically useful, privacy-aware and scenario-targeted synthetic datasets for testing, simulation, analytics, model development and rare-edge-case coverage.

Problem: teams need realistic data but real production data may be unavailable, sensitive, sparse, biased or missing rare failure cases.

Value: safer test/development data, faster scenario creation, broader edge-case coverage and explicit fidelity/privacy evidence rather than fake records with unknown usefulness.

## Complete product tree

Tabular Generator; Event/Time-Series Generator; Text Synthetic Data; Image Generator; Audio/Speech Generator; Video Generator; Log/Telemetry Generator; Transaction/Behavior Simulator; Rare-Case Generator; Scenario Builder; Constraint/Rules Engine; Privacy Risk Evaluator; Fidelity Evaluator; Bias/Fairness Evaluator; Dataset Versioning; Dataset Marketplace/Pack Library; Test-Fixture API; Model-Training Dataset Builder; Benchmark Dataset Builder; Digital-Twin/Simulation Adapter; API/SDK/CLI; Private/Self-Hosted Edition; Industry Packs; Managed Synthetic Data Service.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree

Features: schema import, distributions, correlations, constraints, relational integrity, temporal patterns, rare-event rates, conditional generation, seed/version reproducibility, scenario parameters, labels/ground truth, privacy metrics, similarity/leakage checks, utility tests, bias analysis, provenance, generation model/version, dataset licenses, export formats and approval gates.

Customers: software teams, QA, data science, AI/ML teams, analytics groups, security teams, researchers, SaaS vendors, enterprises, regulated organizations, simulation providers and developers.

Verticals: finance-like transaction testing, healthcare administrative data, ecommerce/retail, insurance claims simulation, manufacturing/IoT, cyber telemetry, logistics, customer support, autonomous systems, software testing. Sensitive domains need domain-specific privacy/utility evaluation.

## Brain capability tree / architecture

Brain may help infer scenario requirements, create generation plans and identify missing edge cases. Deterministic schema/constraint/privacy/fidelity tests must gate acceptance. Generative models can produce data but cannot claim anonymization or privacy safety without measurable evidence.

Architecture: schema/ontology registry, generation recipe DSL, model/provider router, deterministic simulators, probabilistic/statistical models, constraint solver, privacy attack/evaluation suite, fidelity/utility benchmark engine, seed/version registry, object storage, provenance/evidence ledger and secure isolated workspaces.

## Agent tree

Schema Analyst; Scenario Designer; Generator Agent; Rare-Case Agent; Constraint Agent; Privacy Evaluator; Fidelity Evaluator; Bias/Fairness Agent; Dataset QA Agent; Benchmark Agent; Pack Curator; Documentation Agent; Cost/Compute Optimizer.

## Deterministic services

Schema validation; relational key generation; constraint solver; seed management; reproducibility; statistical comparison; privacy leakage tests; duplication/memorization checks; dataset hashing/versioning; licensing metadata; generation quotas; sandboxing and export controls.

## Workflow tree

Define use case → classify sensitivity → import/define schema and constraints → select generator/simulator → define fidelity/privacy targets → generate candidate → validate structure → run privacy/leakage/utility/bias tests → reject/regenerate or approve → version/hash/package dataset → export only under policy → monitor downstream performance and regenerate when assumptions change.

## Integrations / API / data

Databases/warehouses, schemas/data catalogs, ML platforms, notebooks, CI/QA, test frameworks, feature stores, simulation engines, object storage and privacy tooling. APIs for schemas, recipes, generation jobs, scenarios, evaluations, datasets and provenance.

Data: schemas, generation recipes, seeds, model/provider refs, synthetic records/media, evaluation metrics, privacy/fidelity evidence and dataset lineage. Raw source data must be minimized and isolated.

## Monetization / distribution

Rows/records, generation jobs, compute, datasets, storage, API usage, industry packs, private deployment, seats, enterprise, managed services and marketplace licensing. Distribution via AI/data/QA developer ecosystems and enterprise data/privacy partners.

## Security/privacy/compliance

Primary risk is accidental memorization/re-identification. Require source isolation, secrets/PII classification, privacy tests, access control, data minimization, no unsupported anonymization claims, generation provenance and controlled exports. Domain/legal review may be needed for regulated data.

## Failure / edge cases

Memorized source rows, unrealistic correlations, mode collapse, broken referential integrity, impossible timestamps, privacy leakage, underrepresented edge cases, biased labels, overfit benchmarks, synthetic artifacts that make tests too easy, generator drift, nondeterministic reproduction. Quality targets must be explicit per use case.

## Scale / overlap

Test fixtures → enterprise synthetic data → simulation/data-generation infrastructure. Overlap #65 QAaaS, #3 AI quality, #76 PII discovery, #77 redaction, #94 lineage. #056 owns generated replacement/simulation data.

## Classification

**DESIGN NOW:** provenance/version/seed identity, sensitivity classification, provider isolation, evaluation/evidence contracts, resource quotas.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center Brain/Artifact/Evaluation/Resource Governor interfaces should support generated datasets and reproducibility.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** recipe/schema registry, privacy/fidelity evaluation, isolated storage and compute routing.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** generation models, industry packs, marketplace, customer connectors/pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** distributed generation farms, large multimodal simulation and marketplace network.
